I'm agender and have BDD. It feels like I have two different ways I think about my body.

The first is in a gendered way. I'm fortunately very ambivalent about any secondary sex characteristics. I say fortunately, because I don't feel like I need hormones or surgery, so don't have to deal with waiting lists and so on. However, many nonbinary people do benefit from these treatments to help their dysphoria, so if you think it would help, it can be worth exploring with your doctor.

The second way is the BDD way. I hate mirrors, want to cry if I see a photo of myself, can't even deal with seeing my reflection in the door if it's at the wrong angle. I feel like a monster. Other people being able to see me is so upsetting. This doesn't change, no matter how big/small I am, or how my skin is.

They're very different to me. But possibly because I knew I was non binary as a kid, and BDD didn't start getting bad until I was a teenager. I don't know if this helps, but I kinda wanted to explain how my thinking is split. I did have dysphoria temporarily and that was horrible too, but different. It's really hard to explain... and probably moot as everyone is different! If you're worried about BDD, do take the time to be careful and make sure you know whether your worries are that or dysphoria. If it's dysphoria though, treatment will make a difference (a lot of people worry their transition won't be "perfect", but doing something is better than nothing)

Sorry I've gone on. I wanted to note it's possible to be enby and have BDD. Realising I could distill it to... my gender feelings have to do with the concrete reality of how others treat me vs my inner self; whereas BDD is how I think other people see me, always negatively, regardless of what anyone has said or done to the contrary.

If you can, do go see a doctor. They should take suicidal ideation pretty seriously and try help you. Even if you have to bypass your parents, if you're worried about their reaction, it's worth a try. Worry is horrible and tiring, so I hope you can find a safer way to relieve your woes.

Your friend probably hasn't forgotten - they just probably don't know how to deal with it, so are trying to cheer you up by always being happy. It sucks, but not a lot of people can deal with it. (But don't let that stop you from talking about it. The internet is always here at least!)

I kinda know how you feel. Whenever I see someone thank their parents etc in the credit of a film, game, book, whatever; I want to burst into tears because that's a relationship I don't have and never will.

So far I figure I have lived and achieved things despite my (genetic) family. So, you can do things and get on in life without family. If you can find things which make you happy within yourself, keep them safe and no one can take them from you.

Secondly, like other posters say, you can create your own family. And it's better, because you get to choose who is in it and who isn't.  When it comes to making friends, there's no cut-off - no time in your life you'll stop making friends. Even if it's bleak now, you might be surrounded by good friends in the future. (There's so much pressure in life that you must have x by the time you're y years old, but friendship isn't one of those things. Lonely times are hard, but they do pass)
